newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks could not hold early gains Monday and succumbed to profit-taking.
The blue chip IPC index fell 18.91 points to close at 3,366.22. In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers by 56 to 31.
Volume was a solid 117.4 million shares traded, but four big trades alone accounted for some 33 million shares.
"Stocks were on offer at the close with more profits taken, but I still like the market because it's gathering strength to chalk up further gains," said Arturo Lopez, a trader at the Arka brokerage.
Analysts put the relatively slow trade down to foreign investors staying in the U.S. markets.
"Those who've taken positions here are not going to move, and we see just same-day buy-sell trading in Mexico," said an equity analyst.
"Dealers are taking advantage of returns on the Dow Jones, so volume is thin here," he added.

Market heavyweight Telmex was among the losers, down 50 centavos ($0.06) to 12.04 pesos ($1.52), while its ADRs ended off 7/8 at 30-3/8. Blue-chip glassmaker Vitro also fell, losing 76 centavos ($0.10) to 14.74 pesos ($1.87).
Technical analysts said the IPC had rebounded close to support at 3,350 points.
Dealers said Monday evening's primary bond auction barely affected trade as rates were expected to change marginally.
